_comment: Portfolio backlog for /agent-loop. Spans THREE repos around one thesis: anvil-engine is the self-hosted agentic browser that BOTH products run on (no Browserbase/Browserless/Steel). Each iteration: STAGE 0 triage across all streams -> do the single highest-leverage item -> verify -> commit/push -> REFILL (append >=1 new next-step you discovered). STOP only if truly nothing + refill yielded nothing.
thesis: anvil-engine (self-hosted CDP browser) is shared infra. Relay = consumer text-a-bot on anvil. DataFaucet = dev/MCP layer; its capture flow still pays Browserbase — moving it to anvil unifies the stack and removes the vendor. Synergy: one browser engine, two products, zero browser vendor.

repos.relay: C:/Users/acwic/relay (awictor/relay, branch main) — consumer Telegram agent. MVP DONE + live-verified.
repos.datafaucet: C:/Users/acwic/mcp-forge (awictor/mcp-forge, master) — DO NOT touch master. All work on branch anvil-migration behind a feature flag; prod stays on Browserbase until Alex merges.
repos.anvil: C:/Users/acwic/anvil-engine (awictor/anvil-engine, main) — the shared browser engine.

invariants: Free services only. Never commit secrets (.env gitignored; grep staged diff before push).

DataFaucet: NEVER commit to master. Use branch 'anvil-migration'; gate every behavior change behind an env flag (e.g. BROWSER_BACKEND=anvil|browserbase, default browserbase) so prod is unaffected until merge.
Verify before done: tsc + tests each repo; real e2e (anvil live at http://localhost:3000) when possible; report call-tested honestly.
$? after a pipe is the pipe's status. Context-mode hook blocks curl — use ctx_execute(fetch) for HTTP probes.
EVERY iteration must REFILL: append >=1 concrete next-step to items[] before finishing, so the loop never dead-ends.

streams.synergy: Wire DataFaucet capture-flow (auto-scan) to anvil as an alternative browser backend behind BROWSER_BACKEND flag. This is the flagship cross-product work — deep well: adapter, session mgmt, live-view, tests, parity with Browserbase.
streams.relay: Extend Relay: more channels (SMS/WhatsApp), richer tools, memory persistence, deploy hardening. Also: dogfood — could Relay consume a DataFaucet-hosted MCP?
streams.anvil: Harden the shared engine: whatever both consumers need (stability, stealth, session limits, observability). Fixes here benefit both products.

Graceful shutdown: on SIGTERM/SIGINT (docker stop, pm2 restart) the long-poll worker should stop getUpdates, flush the in-flight memory.persist, and exit 0 — so a redeploy never drops a half-written memory file or an in-progress reply. Add a signal handler in index.ts; unit-test the shutdown fn (mock the poller + memory). Real 24/7 resilience, not cosmetic.
